Agentic Enterprise

items.text:
Codifix is the plumbing and electrical wiring
for the Agentic Enterprise.

Your platforms keep their interfaces.
Codifix does the integration.
Connect existing AI platforms, agents and enterprise expertise.

notes:
Founder-selected positioning: Codifix supplies the infrastructure for an Agentic Enterprise. The plumbing and electrical wiring phrase is a metaphor for reusable connections, knowledge and governance. The goal is easier and lower-risk transformation; no measured risk reduction, universal connector coverage or productivity claim is implied. Knowledge/governance remains the foundation, broad platform integration the product direction. Platform-native adapters allow external systems to keep supported interfaces; Codifix builds the integration and maps authorization explicitly. Configuration, authentication and permission mapping remain necessary. No new standard must be adopted by the external platform. This is an investor discussion deck, not an offer or fixed fundraising ask. The Tom briefing is pre-meeting research only; no conversation, feedback, endorsement or investment interest is claimed.

notes:
Architectural direction: external platforms use their own supported interfaces; Codifix implements adapters. The diagram does not establish that every API/MCP platform has a shipped connector or that credentials/permissions transfer automatically. Vertices are independently administered units, each with local knowledge and agents. Authorized edges exchange selected expertise. ATProto sits between Codifix network components, not as a new interface requirement imposed on Databricks or every external platform. Private Q&A still uses the Memory gateway; it is not placed in the PDS or publication log. ATProto Lexicons describe records, RPC endpoints and events; XRPC defines the wire conventions and service authentication. These extension points do not provide arbitrary enterprise-policy semantics. Memory owns disclosure, authorization and operational history. title: Databricks plugs into the network

items.text: Cited answer returns to the existing agent

Payment latency: check the permitted runbook.
A responder acts; the source team reviews corrections for later reuse.
No platform rewrite or ATProto adoption. Connector configuration still required.
Databricks external MCP documentation · integration not yet verified

notes:
Illustrative consumer path: Databricks agent → Unity Catalog registered MCP Service and HTTP connection → Codifix Streamable HTTP MCP interface → permitted private Memory expertise Q&A → cited answer. Databricks is a consumer, not a live federated data source in this example. The incident and expected answer are fictional; no deployment, affiliation or customer outcome is claimed. No Databricks-specific connector or end-to-end test was found. No platform rewrite or ATProto adoption is required by this proposed route, but endpoint reachability, TLS/network configuration, scoped credential mapping and a consent/citation test remain necessary.
Databricks requires Streamable HTTP, a Unity Catalog enabled workspace, supported model-serving region and reachability from serverless compute over permitted public/private networking. Invocation requires EXECUTE and USE CATALOG/SCHEMA; restrict USE CONNECTION to service authors/admins because direct connection use can bypass service restrictions. Stored Bearer credentials are supported, alongside OAuth options. Shared credentials do not propagate a person's identity or authorize onward model disclosure. Confirm target cloud/account availability. Native agent-use documentation is Public Preview; service policies have their own Beta status. Do not imply the entire integration path is GA.
Memory has scoped Bearer/x-api-token HTTP MCP and per-request roles. F1 requires exact-question consent plus operator-bound caller/output destination; read_only=false for ask. An adapter must preserve these requirements, including human confirmation. Correction reuse requires origin review, local curation and renewed collection review; ordinary source memory is not automatically rewritten.

title:
Self-improving knowledge,
with human control

items.text: Implemented and configurable. Quality improvement remains to be measured.
Knowledge maintenance, evidence and review boundaries

notes:
Codifix seeks supporting evidence and preserves reviewable history as knowledge changes. This is implemented, configurable knowledge maintenance, not measured autonomous quality improvement. The diagram shows the enabled, non-dry-run decision paths; it does not claim every check rewrites content or requires human approval.
Prioritize: retrieval, citations and direct reads reinforce activation. This usage signal identifies frequently used knowledge; it is not proof of correctness. Volatility is an EWMA of recorded source-verification status changes, not detection of every changing enterprise fact. Higher volatility brings eligible rechecks forward. Activation thresholds, an existing review flag, cooldown, due time and daily/per-cycle budgets still apply. High volatility with low activation does not trigger evidence gathering or an LLM call.
Automatic validation defaults to off, with dry-run on and auto-apply rewording off. Operators must opt in. Dry-run records evidence and would_* outcomes/cooldown without the diagram's live content/status changes. Source: crates/mem-config/src/pipeline.rs:537; crates/mem-reinforce/src/selection.rs:35; crates/mem-service/src/repository/handlers/reinforcement.rs:216.
Gather evidence: bounded recorded source snippets, provenance verification, one-hop related memories, prior validations and source-path repository history. A strict evidence-reference allowlist rejects unknown references; accepted references do not prove conclusions or calibrate model confidence. Optional manual/API hybrid fallback scans a bounded tracked repository when first-pass evidence is ambiguous or unsupported. No unrestricted web research or mathematical proof. Source: crates/mem-reinforce/src/validate/evidence.rs:71; verdict.rs:131; mod.rs:291.
Decide: clear valid knowledge refreshes validation metadata without a new content version. Ambiguous, unsupported or low-confidence findings set needs_review and leave content unchanged. Flag-only findings are surfaced by scores --needs-review/query flags, not the default pending correction queue. A supported proposed correction is queued separately; an authorized reviewer can apply or reject it. Approval writes an immutable new version while preserving canonical identity/history. The review permission is a service role, not proof of a human identity. Neither flags nor queued proposals currently notify/contact anyone outside Memory. The dashed Next branch is planned proactive human outreach, requiring ownership, channel permissions, acknowledgement and audit design.
Weak evidence does not authorize a rewrite. Explicitly enabled, high-confidence wording-only changes can auto-apply; separate curation policies have their own replacement rules. Do not claim all changes require human approval. Source: crates/mem-reinforce/src/validate/apply.rs:76; mod.rs:350,573; crates/mem-curate/src/repository.rs:570; docs/user/cli/review.md. Cross-unit correction reuse still requires origin/local curation and renewed collection review. Validation quality, missed changes, reviewer time, validation-token cost and subsequent correction reuse remain M3/M5 evidence gates. Architecture explanation: docs/developer/architecture/memory-reinforcement.md.

title:
Connected context. Portable memory.
Traceable corrections.

items.text:
Connected context. Portable memory.
Traceable corrections.

Meaning, keywords and code relationships
find relevant context.

Knowledge persists across supported agent clients
and embedding-model changes.

Sources, version history and review decisions
remain connected.
Implemented strengths. Their combined customer value remains to be measured.
Retrieval, embedding spaces, review and evaluation evidence

notes:
Codifix's distinctive combination is connected retrieval, portable canonical memory and traceable corrections. This describes product focus, not exclusivity or a claim that competitors lack these features.
Connected retrieval: the query pipeline combines semantic similarity, lexical/keyword matching and bounded graph signals. The code graph must be extracted first; memories link through file provenance to symbols and nearby relationships. Semantic retrieval needs populated embeddings. Graph connections explain retrieval but are not standalone answer citations. Answer synthesis exposes evidence sufficiency and validates cited memory IDs. The current retrieval channels run sequentially, so no parallel-retrieval performance claim is made. Sources: docs/user/cli/query.md:41; crates/mem-search/src/lib.rs:377.
Portable memory: canonical content and history are separate from derived vectors. Supported agent clients can use Memory's MCP interfaces. Embedding spaces are keyed by provider, base URL and model; several spaces can coexist. A new space must be populated/backfilled and validated before active use. Switching to an already populated supported space need not recompute existing vectors. Multi-backend creation incurs additional embedding calls. Provider support for embeddings does not imply identical chat-model support, interchangeable database engines or universal platform/model compatibility. Sources: docs/user/cli/embeddings.md; crates/mem-search/src/embedding_backend.rs:37; rebuild.rs:113; lib.rs:150; docs/developer/architecture/mcp-server.md.
Traceable corrections: canonical memory identity connects provenance, review outcomes and immutable versions. Approved factual corrections create a new version; explicitly configured high-confidence wording changes and separate curation policy differ. Signatures establish authenticity/integrity, not factual truth or human approval. Sources: docs/user/cli/review.md; crates/mem-reinforce/src/validate/mod.rs:573; docs/developer/adr/0002-reinforcement-scores-outside-immutable-versions.md.
Implemented: stdio/Streamable HTTP MCP; scoped per-request service authorization; reviewed federation publication/import; version/provenance controls; private gateway Q&A and explicit onward-consent boundary. F1 uses synthetic data, fake provider synthesis and independent databases/HTTP applications in a single test process on one host. The E gate starts independent service executables. These are controlled demonstrations, not customer deployments, customer SSO or a multi-host fleet. Full security, recovery, deployment and evaluation gates remain.
R3 development observation on 17 September: 75/75 executions completed; 60 knowledge answers await genuine blinded human review; 0/15 successful complete coding sequences (one repository family, five conditions, three repeats). execution_valid=true, harness_valid=false, official_evidence=false, quality_passed=false. Deadline/tool/completion-protocol failures do not isolate Memory's coding contribution. No validated quality improvement, perfect recall or token saving is claimed.
Since prior M4, committed protected payload export/import operator and metadata-only area-supervisor inspection add bounded foundations. They do not establish real-data area import, integrated agent execution, release activation or a live four-area demo. Native Spaces adoption and broader delegated execution remain future work.
Sources: docs/reviews/federation-first/f1-execution.md; docs/reviews/federation-first/2026-09-09-e-completion.md; evals/r3/development-continuation-20260917.md; evals/r3/coding-diagnosis-20260917.md; docs/reviews/four-area-network/README.md; docs/developer/architecture/mcp-server.md.

title: Architecture today. Communication tomorrow.

items.text:
Identity + signed records
Extensible schemas and services

Authorization + publication history
Private Q&A through the gateway

Trusted gateway; authorized copies remain readable.
Revocation cannot recall copies. Signatures do not establish truth.
Machine-native agent communication: compatibility, evaluation and auditability first.
ATProto specifications · Memory boundaries · Neuralese research

notes:
ATProto supplies stable identifiers, record schemas, signed repositories and synchronization; custom Lexicon services extend the protocol. It does not automatically supply enterprise policy, truth, immutable audit history or cross-model representation compatibility. Memory enforces authorization, reviewed publication/version history and disclosure. Private expertise Q&A uses the addressed gateway mailbox, outside the PDS, shared publication log and retrieval corpus. Gateway availability/enforcement are trusted dependencies. Authorized gateways/operators/recipients can read and retain content. Revocation denies subsequent gateway operations; already authorized in-flight work may complete and delivered copies cannot be recalled while local authorization permits reading.
Native ATProto Spaces is upstream alpha; Codifix adoption remains deferred, and broader delegated execution remains future work. Do not portray these as completed or production ready.
Neuralese is an application-level research direction: learned/latent inter-agent representations. ATProto can carry extensible data/messages but transport flexibility does not make heterogeneous model representations compatible. No latent-payload feature, token saving, superior quality or Neuralese security guarantee is implemented. Any experiment needs supported participant interfaces, representation compatibility, human-review/audit design, workload/cost and task-quality evaluation. Structured messages are not automatically Neuralese.
Sources: https://atproto.com/specs/lexicon; https://atproto.com/specs/xrpc; https://atproto.com/specs/did; https://atproto.com/specs/repository; https://atproto.com/specs/sync; https://atproto.com/blog/atproto-spaces-alpha; docs/developer/adr/0011-atproto-federation-adapter.md; docs/reviews/federation-first/f1-execution.md; docs/developer/architecture/federation-security.md; docs/future-development/federation-protocol-spike.md:106; https://aclanthology.org/P17-1022/ (Translating Neuralese, primary 2017 research).
